cases.description: Two staggered runs traverse a forward-declared join graph without interleaving an older ready run.
Dependency completion across time jumps does not rewrite downstream creation deadlines.
Case-sensitive run and step IDs remain separate, and underscore is a valid complete identifier.
Graph duplicate IDs are selected before unknown dependency errors.
All command scalar validation happens before a duplicate-run runtime error can occur.
Recover the later in-flight run before starting the earlier run whose deadline became due while down.
A cancelled later run must reconcile its uncertainty before an older due retry executes.
Different creation times produce separate retry deadlines; cancelling a recovered later effect preserves the older success.
One run succeeds and another exhausts an identical budget because only the first loses a transient response.
A second-attempt lost transient is retried with attempt two, then terminal failure preserves an independent success.
At the largest time, exhausting the budget fails normally without computing an overflowing unused deadline.
An exact-bound retry deadline survives a crash and can complete at that time.
Three lost transient responses and a success all belong to one durable attempt even with max_attempts one.
Replay can crash before and after calling the service before cancellation resolves the original recorded effect.
Missing lookups lost after their calls are repeated across cancellation requests and time changes.
An uncertain cancelling run stays uncertain through a pre-lookup crash, passive restart, and ordinary crash.
A cancelled second attempt after a pre-effect crash retains its attempt number and old deadline for lookup.
Cancellation of an applied second attempt can lose its found lookup and repeat it without changing the attempt or deadline.
Cancelling failed and succeeded runs is a no-op beside an already cancelled run, even after a response-loss recovery.
Cancellation after a recovered join effect preserves all successful branches and suppresses its downstream tail.
Exhausting one branch blocks another branch that already consumed an attempt and has its own pending retry.
Cancellation preserves distinct retry deadlines and attempt counts across independently waiting branches.
Starting a duplicate run while down reports process availability before run identity.
An ordinary crash command cannot run after a checkpoint has already taken the process down.
A request can end while down after an effect with durable progress still running and the dependent still pending.
An ID remains reserved after crash recovery reconciles a run as cancelled.
A stale transient must not reopen a replacement success or schedule a retry.
Recovering lost transient responses consumes calls, not new attempt numbers.
Renewal at exact expiration fails and cannot prevent reclamation.
Repeated cancellation must not expire a newly acquired lookup lease.
A lookup response can itself be lost to expiry and recovered without executing.
Mixed found/missing reconciliation drains every running branch and cancels pending children.
Failure draining blocks an unexecuted sibling and cancellation cannot change failing to cancelling.
Draining a failed run does not prevent independent runs from continuing.
Expired running work precedes pending work across run boundaries.
An effect alone cannot release a dependent step.
A worker can reclaim its own expired lease with a new ticket and unchanged attempt.
A response while down cannot commit; after expiry only the replacement may commit.
Old transient delivery cannot reset a newer committed retry deadline.
Time after a successful renewal crosses the new deadline, not the original one.
Unknown delivery tickets are errors.
Ticket ownership remains its original worker even while current.
Down-worker validation precedes unknown-ticket lookup.
A malformed later command wins over an earlier runtime error.
Acquiring a lease must check deadline arithmetic.
Renewal deadline overflow is an error even with a currently live lease.
A committed transient validates retry deadline overflow.
Delivery without a saved response is harmless and leaves the lease usable.
Different run/step tuples cannot collide through delimiter concatenation.
Seeded long interleaving combines recovery, renewal, duplicate/stale messages, retries and terminal draining.
